home.title: Bhote Koshi flood help | npflood.org
home.description: Bhote Koshi flood tools: Nepal emergency contacts, I am safe, looking for family, and a message for people at Gyirong in China. You send the message yourself.
home.lede: What do you need? Choose one. You are not registered here, and we do not keep a list.

status.title: Nepal emergency contacts | npflood.org
status.description: Confirmed Nepal phones for the Bhote Koshi flood: Police 100, fire 101, ambulance 102, Bipad Helpline 1234, National Emergency Operation Centre 1149. This site does not give live road or evacuation status.
status.lede: These are confirmed Nepal phones. This site does not provide live road, border, or evacuation status. Follow DHM and NDRRMA only.

danger.title: Immediate danger | npflood.org
danger.description: If you are in immediate danger, pick Nepal or Gyirong in China. Nepal phones are not local emergency numbers in China.
danger.lede: Pick where you are. Nepal phones are not local emergency numbers in Gyirong, China.

needs.title: Basic supplies and shelter | npflood.org
needs.description: Official desks that take requests for help after the Bhote Koshi flood. This is not a live list of water, shelter, or stock. Contacts appear only when confirmed.
needs.lede: This page lists official desks that take requests for help. This is not a live list of water, shelter, sanitation, or charging stock.

find.title: Looking for someone in Nepal | npflood.org
find.description: If you are in Nepal looking for someone after the Bhote Koshi flood, prepare a note and take it to police, a hospital, or a ward office. This site cannot find anyone.
find.lede: This site cannot find a person. We have no list. Prepare the details below and take them to police, a hospital, or a ward office.

consular.title: Looking for family from abroad | npflood.org
consular.description: If you are abroad looking for family after the Bhote Koshi flood, prepare a note and take it to your embassy or ICRC family links.
consular.lede: You are abroad. Take these details to your embassy or to ICRC Restoring Family Links. We will not invent embassy numbers.

help.title: Volunteer and donate | npflood.org
help.description: How to help after the Bhote Koshi flood. Official donation links, and volunteer coordinators when confirmed. This site does not take money.
help.lede: We do not take volunteer sign-ups. Donation links below go to official organisations. This site does not take money.

safe.lede: A short message for family. You send it yourself by SMS, WhatsApp, or on paper.

faq.a: No. This site does not keep a list of people. You are not registered here.

faq.q: Can this site find a missing person?
faq.a: No. Prepare a note and take it to police, a hospital, a ward office, your embassy, or ICRC Restoring Family Links.

In Nepal: Police 100, fire 101, ambulance 102, Bipad Helpline 1234, National Emergency Operation Centre 1149. In Gyirong (China): no local emergency numbers are listed yet. Do not dial Nepal 100 as local police in China.

faq.q: What do I do with the message this site prepares?
faq.a: Give or send it yourself on paper, SMS, WhatsApp, or WeChat. There is no inbox here.

statusHazard: If you are on the Bhote Koshi or Trishuli floodplain in Nepal, sleep on high ground. A landslide-formed lake upstream could breach. Follow DHM and NDRRMA warnings only, not forwarded messages, including this page.
outOfContact: Out of contact does not mean dead. Roads and phone lines are down. Most people listed as missing are alive and unreachable.
statusBody: These phones are for Nepal, including Rasuwa. Numbers can change. Prefer what a local official tells you on the ground.
If you are in Gyirong (China), do not dial these as local emergency services.
statusChinaLink: Gyirong is in China. Open the danger page, or prepare a Gyirong message.

findBody: A police post or the nearest police office in Nepal. Dial 100.
The nearest hospital or health post.
The ward office, municipality, or district administration office.
consularBody: Call your own country's embassy or consulate. They may have a flood desk.
For Nepali families, watch official Nepal government notices and the Consulate General in Lhasa. Their number will appear on Emergency contacts when it is confirmed.
findListsDisclaimer: These sites are not npflood.org. This site cannot look anyone up. We have no list.
findListPolice: Nepal Police missing and unidentified registers
findListPmo: Government rescue request portal (Office of the Prime Minister). Their counts are theirs, not ours.
aggregatorDisclaimer: This is not a government site. It collects official lists. This site cannot search it.
unofficialDeath: Social media posts, news reports, and family statements are not official confirmation of death or identification.
identificationGate: If authorities have told you identification may be required
dnaTitle: If photo identification is not possible
dnaBody: The Government of Nepal facilitates DNA matching where photo ID fails or remains are temporarily interred. First-degree relatives can send DNA profiles or give blood samples.
consularRemains: A published nine-step process exists for returning foreign nationals' remains, coordinated through embassies. Ask your own embassy. This site does not list the steps.
helpBody: Share the emergency contacts page and this site. Do not spread unconfirmed numbers.
Only trust official organisations for blood, clothes, or money. This site does not take money or bank details.
Do not travel to the flood area to help unless an official coordinator asked you to. Unrequested arrivals use helicopter seats that injured people need.

helpDonations.pmdrf: Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund (official government)

helpHeldBody: Volunteer coordinators will be listed here only when confirmed. This site does not take volunteer sign-ups.
helpNoMail: This site does not take mail. Distressed people should use Emergency contacts, Find, or Consular. Not this page.
helpBuiltBy: This tool was built by Alexandru Budurovici.
trekGuidance: This is for agency staff. Nothing entered here is sent to npflood.org. Drafts stay on this phone only. If the party is safe or the location changes, write that the same way you sent the first note.
